title: Muni 30-Year Yield Highest Since at Least 2011
summary:
Bloomberg's Shruti Singh and Aashna Shah join Emily Graffeo on "Bloomberg Real Yield." A painful fixed-income selloff is eroding returns in state and local government debt, driving the rate on benchmark 30-year municipal bonds above the 5% threshold, the highest since at least January 2011.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Brazil Meat Firm Pauses Bond-Sale Plan as Funding Costs Soar
summary: MBRF Global Foods Co. SA has decided to hold off on a potential junk-debt offering as a global bond selloff has sent borrowing costs soaring.

title: See 'Skittishness' Around Credit: Annie Seelaus
summary:
Annie Seelaus, CEO of R. Seelaus, and John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson, join Emily Graffeo on "Bloomberg Real Yield." The spread on the riskiest US corporate bonds has jumped above 1,000 basis points over Treasuries for the first time since the regional banking crisis in 2023. That level of risk premium typically implies high probability of default, restructuring or loss.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Yields Erases EM Bond Gains
summary:
Tara Hariharan, Co-CIO with NWI Management, joins Emily Graffeo on "Bloomberg Real Yield." Dollar debt from countries in the emerging world has turned negative for the year, after having outperformed as turmoil sent yields on US Treasuries to the highest in nearly two decades.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Economy 'Running Firm', Not Overheating: Roth
summary:
Stephanie Roth, chief economist at Wolfe Research, and Guneet Dhingra, head of US rates strategy at BNP Paribas join Emily Graffeo on "Bloomberg Real Yield." US Treasuries rebounded from the global bond selloff that raced through European markets on Thursday. Earlier in the day, US 10-year yield surged to the highest level since 2002.

 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Iran Offers to Allow Nuclear Inspectors If Sanctions Are Eased

title: Jefferson Says Fed May Need More Time to Decide on Next Move

title: Treasuries Surge as France’s Fiscal Woes Boost Haven Demand

title: Disney's Walden Says Layoffs Are 'Extremely Painful'
summary: Dana Walden, Walt Disney Co.’s president and its first chief creative officer, says the company is not firing people every six months. She does say there is a constant need to look at how an organization is structured and that layoffs are "extremely painful." She speaks to Lucas Shaw at Bloomberg Screentime in Los Angeles. (Source: Bloomberg)
